messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: GeoDNS query error rate spike observed for eu-west-2 resolvers at 2026-03-15T10:23:00Z. Trigger: resolver-mismatch-threshold. Ops channel auto-joined.

maria: Acknowledge. I'm oncall for SRE. Seeing elevated 5xx from inference-api when queries originate via eu-west-2 DNS paths.

jon: Any customer tickets yet?

cust-success: We're seeing two inbound support tickets mentioning timeouts for embeddings endpoints from EU customers. Marking high priority.

maria: Quick check: running `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com` vs `@8.8.8.8` yields different answers intermittently.

jon: paste the dig outputs?

maria: ```
# dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 1234
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.com. 60 IN A 10.40.12.5

# dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 5678
```

ashley: That smells like inconsistent propagation between our Route53 primary and Cloudflare authoritative mirror. Could be TTL mismatch or recent deploy of delegations.

kevin: Confirming — we've pushed a change to NS records for the eu zone ~2h ago to route traffic to new edge. TTLs were 300s but some resolvers cached legacy delegations longer.

maria: Impact assessment: from infra telemetry, ~12% of EU requests hit the NXDOMAIN path within the last 10m causing retries and 503s. Top affected tenants: merchant-42, analytics-suite, and two enterprise trials.

infra-ops: We're seeing a propagation skew: Cloudflare answers A with old IPs for some resolver pools, Route53 already serves new IPs. Also mixed CNAME chaining in zone noted.

jon: Mitigation options?

maria: Immediate mitigations I can run now:
- Rollback NS change (fast) -> risk: may not undo cached delegations
- Add a short-lived A record in Cloudflare matching Route53 to unify answers (fast, manual)
- Increase px routing to us-west temporarily (may increase latency for EU)

ashley: +1 to adding short-lived A in Cloudflare for the affected host. That gives us a uniform answer while caches expire. We should also raise TTLs back to something stable after.

kevin: I'll prepare the Cloudflare patch. Will apply to `api.redwood-inference.com` with 60s TTL and mirror Route53 IPs.

maria: While that's applied, I'll modify our smart routing policy to prefer eu-west-1 and us-west-2 as fallback for the next 30m. This should keep most requests serving.

deploy-bot: deployment triggered by kevin: cf-dns-hotfix -> status: queued

kevin: applied. Patch ID cf-20260315-01, changed A to 10.40.12.5 and 10.40.12.6, TTL=60.

maria: Confirming via live probes: `dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com` now returns A 10.40.12.5 consistently. `dig @8.8.8.8` still shows NXDOMAIN in some regions — cache hasn't expired yet but aggregator traffic now prefers new answers.

cust-success: Notifying affected customers with ETA ~30-45m for full propagation. Drafting outgoing note.

jon: Monitoring — metrics show 5xx rate dropping from 12% -> 4% over last 6m. Good. Keep an eye on error budgets.

maria: I'm going to leave a temporary runbook step set: if 5xx > 8% for 15m, escalate to platform oncall and revert NS change.

ashley: Also scheduling a follow-up: post-incident config review for delegation changes. Need to add a preflight check for mixed CNAME+delegation patterns.

infra-ops: FYI, Cloudflare support case opened (case# CF-764321) to ask about propagation anomalies for EU resolvers. Copying logs.

kevin: Will hold the Cloudflare short-lived A for 1h then set TTL=300 and coordinate with Route53 team to align.

maria: Handing off to ashley for next oncall window at 11:00Z. Ashley, you'll have follow-ups: confirm Cloudflare case resolution, monitor 5xx for another 45m, and coordinate customer comms closure.

ashley: Taking it. I'll add notes to the incident tracker and tag for postmortem.

cust-success: Customers informed. One customer asked for timeline for root cause — we'll say: "intermittent DNS delegation propagation between providers; short-term mitigation applied; full stabilization expected within one hour; detailed postmortem to follow."

maria: Final notes before handoff: root cause hypothesis = concurrent NS delegation change + overlapping CNAMEs caused split-view answers across public resolvers; action items created: 1) preflight checks, 2) align TTLs across providers, 3) document rollback playbook.

ashley: Acknowledged. Closing active paging window. Will keep thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident auto-closed for paging after 45 minutes of degraded signals. Severity: Sev2. Incident ID: INC-20260315-082.

ashley: I'll open the postmortem and assign owners. Thanks all.
